body.p: Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of this application as amended and in view of the following remarks.
Claims 5, 6, 7 and 8 stand objected to because of informalities.
Claims 2-3, 11-12, and 20 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as allegedly
being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which Applicant regards as the invention.
Claims 18-20 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as allegedly being anticipated by U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2021/0173390 to Hosek et al. (hereinafter "Hosek").

Claims 1-4, 7-13, and 16-17 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Hosek in view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2021/0178579 to Saunders et al. (hereinafter "Saunders").

Claims 5-6 and 14-15 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Hosek in view of Saunders and further in view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2018/0272535 to Ogawa et al. (hereinafter "Ogawa").
Claims 1-20 are pending. Claims 1-3, 6-8, 10-12, 15, 18, and 20 are currently
amended. Claims 4-5 and 13-14 are canceled without prejudice. Claims 21-24 are added. No new matter has been added as a result of these amendments.

Applicant thanks the Examiner for the telephonic interview conducted between the Examiner and Applicant's representative on December 18, 2024. The patentability of claims 1-20 with respect to the rejections of the present Office Action was discussed. In particular, the rejections of claims 1 and 18 under 35 U.S.C. §102 and 35 U.S.C.§103 and the Examiner's interpretation of the cited art were discussed. Agreement on the patentability of the claims was not reached. However, proposed amendments were

discussed, which are reflected above. While no specific agreement was reached regarding allowability, the Examiner stated that the proposed amendments overcome the cited art subject to an updated search.
Claims 5, 6, 7 and 8 stand objected to because of informalities. In particular, the Office Action states that:
...each recite the phrase "the controller is to" that appears to be
missing the word "configured" between "is" and "to".
Applicant respectfully submits that claim 5 is currently canceled without

prejudice and claims 6-8 are amended, as indicated above. Applicant respectfully submits that the amendments do not add new matter. Applicant respectfully requests that the objection to claims 5, 6, 7 and 8 be withdrawn.

The Office Action rejects claims 2-3, 11-12, and 20 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as allegedly being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which Applicant regards as the invention. In particular, the Office Action states:
a. Regarding claims 2, 11, and 20 the phrase "slow enough" renders each

claim indefinite because it is a subjective limitation. The specification does not provide any standard for determining the scope of "slow enough". Some objective standard must be provided in order to allow one of ordinary skill in the art to determine the scope of the claim. A claim that requires the exercise of subjective judgments without restriction renders the claim indefinite. In re Musgrave, 431 F.2d
b. Regarding claims 3, 12, and 20 the phrase 'faster than" renders each

claim indefinite because it is a subjective limitation. The specification does not provide any standard for determining the scope of "faster than". Some objective standard must be provided in order to allow one of ordinary skill in the art to determine the scope of the claim. A claim that requires the exercise of subjective judgments without restriction renders the claim indefinite. In re Musgrave, 431 F.2d

Applicant respectfully submits that claims 2-3, 11-12, and 20 have been amended, as indicated above. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claims 2-3, 11-12, and 20 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) be withdrawn.
Response to Rejections under 35 U.S.C. Q 102(a)(1)

Claims 18-20 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as allegedly being anticipated by Hosek. During the Examiner interview, the Examiner agreed that the proposed amendments to claim 18 overcome the current rejection. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claims 18-20 under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) be withdrawn.
Response to Rejections under 35 U.S.C. Q 103

Claims 1-4, 7-13, and 16-17 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Hosek in view of Saunders. During the Examiner interview, the Examiner agreed that the proposed amendments to claim 1 overcome the current rejection. Claim 10 is amended to include similar features as amended claim 1. Applicant respectfully requests the rejection of claims 1-4, 7-13, and 16-17 under 35 U.S.C. §103 be withdrawn.

Claims 5-6 and 14-15 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Hosek in view of Saunders and further in view of Ogawa. Claims 5-6 depend on and include the features of claim 1. Claims 14-15 depend on and include the features of claim 10. As discussed above, the Examiner agreed that the amendments to claim 1 overcome the current rejection. Claim 10 is amended to include similar features as claim 1. Accordingly, Applicant requests that the rejection of claims 5-6 and 14-15 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 be withdrawn.
It is respectfully submitted that the rejections and objections have been overcome in view of the amendments and remarks set forth herein.
If the Examiner believes a telephone interview would expedite the prosecution of this application, the Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned at (650) 433-5800.
If there are any additional charges, please charge them to Deposit Account No.: 50-1358.
Respectfully submitted,
Date: January 16, 2025 /Audrey G. Ogurchak/
